# Dionysius on [Divine Names]

...established above all things. For if all forms of knowledge belong to existing things and are limited to existing things, then that which is **beyond all essence** <term>beyond all essence (hyperousios): Existing in a way that transcends the very category of "being" or "existence" as we understand it.</term> is also set apart from all knowledge.

<margin>t</margin> Indeed, it is superior to every word and every knowledge, and is established altogether above mind and essence. While it **encompasses**, embraces, and anticipates all things, it remains itself completely **ungraspable** to all. There is no perception of it, nor imagination, nor opinion, nor name, nor word; neither touch, nor science.

How then shall our discourse concerning the **Divine Names** be conducted, since the beyond-essential Divinity is demonstrated to be "uncallable" and beyond naming?

But as we said when we were setting forth our *Theological Outlines* <note>original: "theologikas hypotyposeis" — a reference to another work by Dionysius, often considered a lost or perhaps a fictional work used to build his literary persona.</note>: the **One**, the **Unknown**, the **Beyond-Essential**, the **Good itself**—by which I mean the **Trinitarian Unity** <note>original: "triadiken henada" — Dionysius is reconciling the radical "Oneness" (Unity) of God with the Christian doctrine of the Trinity (Three Persons).</note>, equal in divinity and goodness—it is impossible to either speak of or to conceive.

<margin>h</margin>

<margin>A</margin> Moreover, even the **angel-like unions** of the holy powers—whether we should call them "grasps" or "receptions" <gloss>ways of receiving divine light</gloss> of the beyond-unknown and beyond-radiant Goodness—are both unspeakable and unknown. They exist only within those angels who have been deemed worthy of them, who possess a knowledge that transcends the angelic.

<margin>T</margin> The godlike minds, uniting themselves to these unions in imitation of the angels—as far as is possible—do so because this kind of **union** <term>union (henosis): The state of becoming one with God, which Dionysius argues happens only when we stop trying to "think" about God and instead enter a state of silent contemplation.</term> of divinized minds with the **beyond-divine light** occurs during the **cessation** of all intellectual activity. They hymn...

<margin>t</margin>

<summary>Dionysius explains that because God is beyond all being, He is also beyond all human knowledge, language, and perception. He introduces the concept of "divine union" which occurs only when the mind stops its active reasoning, an experience shared by angels and "godlike" human minds.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion on the limitations of human perception, transitioning from the total unknowability of the Divine to the specific ways humans and angels might "see" or "participate" in God—primarily through the "Divine Names" and symbols, eventually reaching toward the "beyond-essential" light.</meta>

### On Divine Names

If we attain this final destination, we shall always be with the Lord, as the holy scripture says.

<margin>T</margin> On the one hand, we are filled with His visible **theophany** <term>theophany: a visible manifestation of God to humanity, such as a vision or a sacred appearance</term> through most pure contemplations, as His presence shines around us with the brightest of rays, just as it did for the disciples during that most divine **Transfiguration** <note>original: "metamorphosei." Dionysius refers to the event on Mount Tabor where Jesus was seen in his divine glory by Peter, James, and John.</note>.

<margin>T</margin> On the other hand, we participate in His intellectual **gift of light** with a mind that is dispassionate and immaterial, and we partake in the union that is beyond the mind through the unknown and blessed reaches of those rays that shine from above. This is done through a more divine imitation of the heavenly minds; for we shall be **equal to the angels** <note>original: "isangeloi." A reference to Luke 20:36, suggesting that in the afterlife, humans will share the same direct mode of knowing as the angels.</note> as the truth of the scripture says, and "sons of God," being sons of the Resurrection.

<margin>N</margin> But for now, as much as is possible for us, we use the symbols that are fitting for divine things. From these symbols, we are raised up—in due proportion to our capacity—toward the simple and unified truth of the spiritual visions. After we have completed every act of understanding that our God-like minds can achieve, we cease our intellectual activities and reach out, as far as is permitted, toward the **beyond-essential ray** <term>beyond-essential ray (hyperousion aktina): the light of God that transcends the very definition of "being" or "existence."</term>. In this ray, all the boundaries of all knowledge pre-exist in a way that is beyond all words. It is impossible to think of this ray, to describe it, or to observe it in any way at all, because it is set apart from all things and is **utterly beyond knowing** <note>original: "hyperagnoston." This is a central theme of "apophatic" or negative theology: God is so far beyond us that He is best described by what He is NOT.</note>. It has pre-enfolded within itself all the limits of all knowledge and powers that belong to the world of being, doing so in a way that is beyond being itself, with a power that is entirely unmasked—and [the power] of the heavenly minds...

<summary>Dionysius explains that while God is beyond all knowledge, humans can approach Him through "fitting symbols" and "theophanies" (like the Transfiguration) until they eventually transcend intellectual activity to reach the "beyond-essential ray."</summary>
<keywords>Theophany, Transfiguration, Divine Names, beyond-essential, apophatic theology, angel-like, Resurrection, hyperousios</keywords>

<margin>A</margin>nd as the **Cause** of all beings: since all things were brought into existence because of His essence-making goodness. <note>original: "ousiopoion agathotēta." This refers to God's "goodness" not just as a moral quality, but as the creative force that gives "essence" or "being" to everything that exists.</note>

<margin>W</margin>ise and **Beautiful**: because all beings, by preserving the integrity of their own particular natures, are filled with every divine harmony and sacred elegance.

**Lover of Humanity** <note>original: "philanthrōpon." A traditional title for God in Greek theology, emphasizing His deep affection and kinship with the human race.</note> in a unique way: because He truly and completely shared in our condition through one of His **persons** <term>persons: translated from "hypostases," referring to the distinct identities within the Trinity; here specifically referring to the Son becoming human</term>, calling us back to Himself and restoring the lowliness of human nature.

The Eternal One took on a temporal duration; He who surpasses every order of every nature in a **beyond-essential** <term>beyond-essential: "hyperousios," a key term for Dionysius meaning that God's "being" is so high it cannot be categorized as "existence" in the way we understand it</term> way came within our human nature, while yet remaining in the unchanging and unconfused stability of His own properties.

And whatever other **theurgic** <term>theurgic: "theourgika," referring to "God-working" or divine acts that have the power to transform or deify the believer</term> lights the secret tradition of our divine teachers has revealed to us—in accordance with the Scriptures—into these we also have been initiated. 

For now, we are led in due proportion through the **sacred veils** <note>original: "hierōn parapetasmantōn." This refers to the symbols, rituals, and language of the Church which "cover" the blinding light of divine truth so that human eyes can bear it.</note> of the love for humanity found in the Scriptures and the hierarchical traditions. This grace wraps spiritual things in sensible forms, and things beyond-being in things that exist. It assigns shapes and types to things that have no shape or type, and multiplies and fashions the supernatural and formless simplicity through the variety of divided symbols. 

But then, when we become incorruptible and immortal, and reach the **Christ-like** and blessed...

For those <margin>3</margin> being led up to Him, He is the uplifting guidance of a hand; for those being illuminated, He is enlightenment. # Dionysius
<note>original: "Διονυσίου περὶ θείων ὀνομάτων" — Dionysius <unclear>on the divine names</unclear></note>

...as if casting themselves upon Him in a manner fitting for the sacred. They neither arrogantly attempt what is impossible for them—going beyond the **divine manifestation** <term>divine manifestation: "theophany," an appearance of God that can be perceived by the mind or senses</term> which is harmoniously granted to them—nor do they slip toward the lower depths through a decline toward the worse. Instead, they stretch themselves out toward the ray shining upon them, steadily and without wavering. Through a love that is proportional to the sights of the divine illuminations, and with a holy reverence, they are "given wings" <note>This is a nod to Plato's "Phaedrus," suggesting the soul grows wings to fly back to its divine source</note> in a temperate and holy way.

<margin>3</margin> Following these **divine-ruling** <note>original: "thearchikois"</note> scales, which also govern the entire sacred arrangement of the heavenly Ranks, we honor the hidden nature of the **Divine Principle** <note>original: "thearchia"</note>—which is beyond mind and essence—with unsearchable and sacred reverences of the mind. Honoring those things that cannot be spoken with a wise silence, we stretch ourselves out toward the rays shining upon us in the **sacred scriptures** <note>original: "logiois," literally "sacred oracles" or "words."</note>. By them, we are led toward the light of the divine-ruling hymns, being illuminated by them in a way that is beyond this world. We are shaped by these sacred songs of praise so that we might see the divine-ruling lights which are given to us in a measured way through them. We then praise the Good-giving Source of every sacred **manifestation of light** <term>manifestation of light: "photophania," the revealing of divine truth through the metaphor of light</term>, just as the Source has revealed concerning itself in the sacred scriptures. 

For instance: that it is the Cause, the Principle, the Essence, and the Life of all things. For those who fall away from it, it is a **calling back** <term>calling back: "anaklēsis," a summons to return to one's original state</term> and a resurrection; for those who have slipped toward the corruption of the divine form, it is a renewal and a **re-formation** <term>re-formation: "anamorphōsis," the process of being shaped back into the divine likeness</term>.

The Good that is beyond word is unspoken by any word; a unity that unifies every unity, and a **supersubstantial essence** <term>supersubstantial essence: "hyperousios ousia," a key term for Dionysius meaning a way of being that is above and beyond what we normally call "existence" or "substance"</term>; and a mind without thought, and a word that cannot be spoken, an absence of word and an absence of thought and a namelessness. # EPIGRAM ON THE BLESSED
# DIONYSIUS REGARDING THE 
# [BOOK] ON DIVINE
# NAMES.

Having dipped God-written lips into a radiant mind,
Painting the varied, sacredly-named beauties, even after death
He sounds forth God-revealing hymns in life-wise words. <note>This poem praises the author, Dionysius, suggesting his writings are divinely inspired and continue to offer wisdom even after his passing.</note>

Now, O blessed one, after the *Theological Outlines* <note>original: "theologikas hypotyposes." This refers to a previous work by the author (now lost or considered part of his literary persona) that dealt with the fundamental nature of the Trinity.</note>, we shall proceed, as far as we are able, to the explanation of the **Divine Names**. Let the law of the **scriptures** <note>original: "logiōn," literally "oracles." Dionysius uses this term to refer to the Bible as a collection of divine utterances.</note> be established for us now as before: that we must be bound to the truth of what is said concerning God. [This is] not in persuasive words of human [wisdom...] <note>original: "peithois sophias anthrō[pinēs]." A reference to 1 Corinthians 2:4, where St. Paul contrasts human rhetoric with the power of the Holy Spirit.</note>

<summary>This page serves as the formal opening of Dionysius's influential work, beginning with a commemorative poem and setting the methodological ground rule: all discussion of God must be rooted in the Holy Scriptures rather than human philosophy.</summary>

# THE CELESTIAL HIERARCHY <note>original: "ouranias ierarchias"</note>

Let this much be said concerning the sacred representations <note>original: "anaplaseōn." In Dionysian theology, these are the symbolic forms or "sculpted" images used in scripture to help the human mind visualize immaterial beings like angels.</note>. Though they fall short of a precise manifestation <note>original: "ekphantorias," a revealing or making shine forth.</note> of those beings, they contribute, I think, toward preventing us from remaining lowly and stuck within figurative imaginings.

**I**f you should also say this—that we have not made mention of all the angelic powers <note>original: "dynameōn," a specific rank of angels but also a general term for their capacities.</note>, activities, or images in order as they appear in the scriptures—we shall answer with the truth: that regarding some, we are ignorant of their super-worldly knowledge <note>original: "hyperkosmion epistēmēn," referring to knowledge that exists beyond the physical universe.</note>; and indeed, in those matters, we ourselves require another to lead us to the light and to initiate us. Other things we have omitted because they possess the same power as what has already been said; we have done this to maintain the proportion of the discourse, and to honor with silence that hiddenness <note>original: "kryphiotēta." This is a central theme in the author’s "apophatic" or negative theology, where God and the highest heavens are best described by what they are not, or by silence.</note> which is beyond us.

### OF DIONYSIUS CONCERNING THE... <note>The title is completed from the previous page: "The Celestial Hierarchy."</note>

<margin>T</margin>he **chariots** represent the yoked fellowship <note>original: "koinōnian," a community or communion.</note> of those of the same rank. The **wheels**, being winged and moving forward without turning or deviating, signify the power of their forward-moving activity along a straight and direct path; their entire intellectual track <note>original: "noeras trochias"</note> is guided in a way that is beyond this world <note>original: "hyperkosmiōs"</note> along the same unwavering and straight-cut road.

<margin>I</margin>f we should also, according to another uplifting interpretation <term>anagoge: the process of being led from physical symbols to spiritual or divine truths</term>, purify the iconographic description of the intellectual wheels: for they were called, as the theologian <note>Likely referring to the prophet Ezekiel, whom Dionysius often calls "the theologian."</note> says, **Gelgel**. In the Hebrew tongue, this signifies "revolutions" and "revelations." For the fiery and God-like wheels possess, by their "revolutions," a movement in eternity around the same Good; and by their "revelations," they manifest hidden things, lifting up those who are earthbound <note>original: "peripeziōn," literally those who travel on foot or on the ground.</note>, and conveying the high illuminations down to the lower orders by a descending transmission.

<margin>R</margin>emaining for our clarification is the discourse concerning the **joy** of the heavenly orders. For they are completely incapable of experiencing our passion-driven pleasure. However, they are said to "rejoice with God" over the finding of those who were lost, according to a God-like ease and a benevolent and ungrudging gladness for the providence and salvation of those who turn toward God. They experience that ineffable well-being <note>original: "eupatheian," a state of "right-feeling" or intellectual joy, contrasted with "pathos" or irrational passion.</note> in which even sacred men have often participated during the God-working <term>theurgy: "God-working" or divine action; the process by which divine light is communicated to humans</term> visitations of the divine illuminations. So much for me concerning the... <note>The text ends mid-sentence; the catchword indicates the next word is "of the..."</note>

## THE CELESTIAL HIERARCHY

**<margin>T</margin>**he symbolism of the **horses** represents their submissiveness and obedience to divine rule. Those that are **white** signify brightness and that which is most closely related to the **divine light** <note>original: "theiou phōtos"</note>. The **dark blue** ones signify the hidden nature <note>original: "to kryphion"</note> of the divine. The **red** horses represent the fiery and active power; and the **dappled** ones—composed of white and black—represent the power that connects the extremes through a mediating faculty <note>original: "diaporthmeutikē dynamei," a power that acts as a ferry or bridge between two points.</note>, joining the first orders to the second, and the second back to the first, either by a reciprocating or a providential bond. If we were not aiming for a balanced brevity in this discourse, we would have applied all the specific characteristics of these animals and all their physical forms to the heavenly powers according to the principle of **dissimilar similarities** <term>anomoious homoiotētas: the theological method of using "unlike" images (like animals) to describe God or angels to remind the reader that the divine is beyond any physical description</term>.

**<margin>T</margin>**he **spirited nature** <note>original: "thymoeides," the irascible or "angry" part of the soul in Greek philosophy.</note> of these animals refers to a spiritual courage, of which our earthly anger is but a faint and distant echo. Their **desire** <note>original: "epithymian"</note> refers to the **divine love** <note>original: "theion erōta"</note>. To speak concisely: we must elevate all the senses and various parts of these irrational animals toward the immaterial perceptions and unified powers of the heavenly beings. This explanation is sufficient for the wise; not only these examples, but even the purification <note>Dionysius uses "purification" to mean the stripping away of the literal meaning to find the spiritual truth.</note> of a single obscure image is enough to clarify all similar figures. We must also examine why **rivers**, **wheels**, and **chariots** are said to be associated with the heavenly beings.

**<margin>F</margin>**or the **rivers of fire** <note>original: "empyrioi potamoi"</note> signify the **God-ruling channels** <note>original: "thearchikous ochetous"</note>, which supply the heavenly beings with an abundant and unfailing flow of life-giving and nourishing fertility.

<summary>Dionysius explains the symbolic meaning of horses of different colors and how the physical traits and passions of animals represent higher spiritual realities and divine streams of life.</summary>
<keywords>celestial hierarchy, horses, divine light, dissimilar similarities, divine love, rivers of fire, angelic symbolism, intellectual courage</keywords>

### [From] Dionysius, Concerning the [Celestial Hierarchy]

...light-like and heavenly radiance. The **bronze** color, following the explanations already given, or the **fiery** and **golden** hues, should be assigned [to these powers]. We should understand that the **multicolored** appearances of precious stones signify different qualities: **white** for the light-like, **red** for the fiery, **yellow** for the golden, and **green** for youth and vigorous health. In every specific type of image, you will find an **anagogical** <term>anagōgikēn: the spiritual process of "leading up" or elevating the soul from physical symbols to divine truths</term> purification of these symbolic representations.

<margin>Α</margin>
But since I believe enough has been said on these matters according to our ability, we must move on to the sacred interpretation of the animal shapes that serve as holy symbols for the **heavenly intellects** <note>Dionysius uses the term "intellects" (noōn) to refer to the angels as purely spiritual beings.</note>.

<margin>Κ</margin>
One should consider that the form of the **lion** manifests a sovereign, strong, and indomitable nature. It also represents the effort to imitate—as far as possible—the hiddenness of the unspeakable **Godhead** <term>thearchias: the "source of divinity," referring to the Trinity as the origin of all power and rule</term>. This is shown by the "veiling of intellectual footprints" <note>original: "perikalypsi." This refers to an ancient belief that lions used their tails to sweep away their tracks to hide from hunters, symbolizing how God remains hidden even while moving through creation.</note> and the mystical, quiet concealment of the upward path that leads toward God through divine illumination. The form of the **ox** signifies strength, vigor, and the ability to widen the "intellectual furrows" to receive the heavenly and life-giving rains <note>In this metaphor, the angel "plows" the soul so it can be "fertilized" by divine grace.</note>. Its **horns** represent a protective and unconquerable power. The form of the **eagle** represents a royal, high-soaring, and swift-flying nature. It signifies the keenness, sobriety, agility, and cleverness in seeking out life-giving nourishment. Most importantly, it represents the ability to gaze directly and unwaveringly, with strong and healthy vision, toward the abundant and many-lighted rays of the **divine sun-burst** <note>According to ancient natural history, the eagle was the only animal capable of looking directly at the sun without blinking or being blinded.</note>.

For this also bears the image and type of **divine energy**, as we have demonstrated at length in our *Symbolic Theology* <note>Dionysius frequently refers to his own (now lost or perhaps fictional) work titled "Symbolic Theology" to explain physical metaphors for God.</note> regarding the purification of the four elements. They receive the first manifestation of light without revealing its secret source, and they pass it on abundantly to the lower orders in a secondary way, according to the capacity of those beings. Indeed, it signifies that within them resides a fertile, life-giving, increasing, and perfecting power, according to their **intellectual rain-bearing** <term>ombrotokian: the spiritual "birthing of rain," where divine wisdom descends like showers to nourish and "grow" lower beings</term>. This calls forth vital "birth-pangs" in the receptive womb of the earth with gentle showers.

It also reflects the luminous and bright quality—as symbolized by **silver**—and...

# On the [Celestial Hierarchy] of Dionysius

...so that it is gathered together in a unified way; and in a circle, with **order**, it revolves around itself in unchanging identity.

**The staffs**, moreover, signify the kingly and ruling authority, and that which brings all things to their divine completion.

**The spears and the axes** signify the power of dividing things that are unlike, and the sharpness, energy, and activity of the powers of discernment.

**The geometrical and building tools** signify the power of founding, building, and perfecting; and whatever else belongs to the uplifting and returning **providence** <note>original: "pronoia." Some signify corrective discipline or punishing justice; others signify freedom from hardship, the conclusion of discipline, the restoration of previous well-being, or the addition of further gifts, whether small or 
<margin>I</margin>

### On the Celestial Hierarchy

...of the powers. Their **feet** signify the mobility, sharpness, and swiftness of their ever-moving journey toward divine things. For this reason, theology <note>The author uses "theology" to refer to the Holy Scriptures, which describe the appearance of angels.</note> has fashioned the feet of these holy minds as winged. 

The **wing** indicates the sharpness of their upward progress, their heavenly nature, and their ability to forge a path toward the heights. It also represents how they are removed from everything lowly and earth-bound because of their "upward-carrying" quality. The **lightness of the wings** shows that they are in no way weighed down by earthly things, but are instead led toward the heights in a way that is entirely pure and unburdened. 

The **nakedness and bare feet** <note>Angels are often depicted as barefoot in Byzantine and early Christian art to show their detachment from the material world.</note> represent that which is free, unhindered, and unconstrained. It signifies a state that is pure and free from any external additions, striving for the closest possible likeness to divine simplicity.

<margin>A</margin> 
But since the **simple yet many-colored Wisdom** <note>original: "polypoikilos sophia." This refers to the "manifold wisdom of God" mentioned in the New Testament (Ephesians 3:10).</note> also clothes these bare beings and gives them various instruments, let us unfold the meaning of the sacred garments and tools of the celestial minds as far as we are able.

<margin>T</margin> 
I believe the **shining and fiery garments** signify the God-like nature <term>theoeides: meaning "God-form" or possessing the characteristics of the Divine</term> based on the image of fire. They also represent the power of illumination, as angels dwell in heaven where light is found, and where everything is intellectually enlightened. 

The **priestly garments** <note>Refers to the liturgical robes often seen on angels in visions, such as those in the book of Revelation.</note> signify the power to lead others toward divine and mystical visions, and the fact that their entire existence is consecrated to God.

<margin>T</margin> 
The **belts** signify the protection of their fertile powers and their unifying habit <note>In this context, "habit" refers to a stable state of being or a focused spiritual disposition.</note>...

# The Celestial Hierarchy

-> **On the Celestial Hierarchy** <-

...[fire] is invisibly ignored and seems not to exist, but through friction—as if by a kind of searching—it suddenly appears in a way that is natural and familiar. Yet just as quickly, it withdraws in an incomprehensible way. It remains undiminished throughout all its most blessed communications of itself. Indeed, one could find many properties of fire that serve as fitting sensory images of the <term>divine-ruling activity</term> <note>original: "thearchikes energeias." This refers to the active, creative, and sustaining operation of God's power throughout the universe.</note>.

**K**nowing this, the **God-wise** <note>original: "theosophoi." This refers to the sacred writers of the Bible and the theologians who interpreted divine mysteries.</note> fashion the **heavenly beings** <note>original: "ouranias ousias." Literally "heavenly essences," the angels.</note> out of fire, illustrating their likeness to God and their ability to imitate Him as far as is possible.

**F**urthermore, they describe them in **human form**. This is due to the human capacity for intellect and the way our visual powers are directed upward, as well as the straight and upright nature of our stature, and our natural capacity for leadership and governance. Although humans may seem the weakest in physical sensation compared to the powers of irrational animals, they dominate all things by the superior power of the mind, the mastery of rational knowledge, and the naturally free and unconquered state of the **soul**.

**I** believe we can also find harmonious images for the heavenly powers within each of our many physical parts. We might say that our **visual powers** represent the clearest upward-gaze toward the divine lights; they also signify a reception of the <term>divine-ruling illuminations</term> <note>original: "thearchikon ellampseon." The spiritual "light" or wisdom that flows from the Godhead into the minds of angels and humans.</note> that is gentle, fluid, and unresisting—moving swiftly, remaining pure, and staying wide open without being affected by worldly passion.

<summary>Dionysius explains how fire and the human body serve as metaphors for angelic nature, specifically how the human form represents the angels' intellectual dominance and their receptivity to divine light.</summary>
<keywords>celestial hierarchy, fire metaphor, human form, divine illumination, angelic intellect, soul, God-wise</keywords>

# Dionysius on the

-> **On the Celestial Hierarchy** <-

...that even the highest Seraphim themselves are "burners," as their name makes clear <note>The name "Seraphim" comes from the Hebrew root *saraph*, meaning "to burn."</note>, and [scripture] assigns to them the property and energy of fire. It is illuminating with its revelatory brilliance; it is uncontainable, unmixed, and discerning. It is unchangeable and upward-tending, swift in its passage, and high, tolerating no downward sinkings. It is ever-moving, self-moving, and moves other things. It encompasses all but cannot be encompassed; it needs nothing else. It grows itself secretly and manifests its own majesty to the materials that receive it. It is active, powerful, and present to all...

...[otherwise] the matter would be absurd and full of much confusion.

<margin>E</margin> But if we say that the same beings both **exercise hierarchy** <note>original: "hierarchein," to act as a leader or sanctifier within the sacred order.</note> and **are subject to hierarchy** <note>original: "hierarcheisthai," to be led or sanctified by a higher rank.</note>, we do not mean this in relation to the same beings or by the same beings. Instead, we mean that each rank is subject to the hierarchy of those who come before it, and it exercises hierarchy over those who follow it. Thus, one might reasonably say that the <term>sacredly-fashioned</term> <note>original: "hieroplastous," referring to symbols or forms created by the Holy Spirit in scripture to represent divine truths.</note> forms found in the **holy oracles** <note>The "logia," a common term for the Holy Scriptures.</note> can be appropriately and truly attributed at different times to the first, the middle, and the last powers. 

For the capacity to be directed upward toward the heights without turning back, the steadfast commitment to their own protective powers, and the participation in the <term>providential power</term> <note>original: "pronoētikēs dynameōs," the power of God's foresight and care for the universe.</note> through their communicative procession to the lower ranks—all these qualities truly apply to all the celestial beings. This remains true even if, as has been said many times, these qualities belong to some in a superior and universal way, and to others in a partial and subordinate way.

<margin>A</margin> We must now state and investigate, in our first <term>purification of the symbols</term> <note>original: "tōn typōn anakatharsei," the process of stripping away the literal meaning of a symbol to reach the spiritual truth behind it.</note>, the reason why **theology** <note>In this context, "theology" refers to the Holy Scriptures themselves.</note> is found to honor the <term>fiery sacred writing</term> <note>original: "empyrion ierographian," the use of fire-based imagery in biblical descriptions.</note> almost above all others. You will find that scripture does not only fashion fiery wheels, but also fiery living creatures, and men who flash like lightning. It places heaps of burning coals around the celestial beings themselves and describes rivers of fire flowing with an unrestrained roar; it even says that the **Thrones** <note>One of the nine choirs of angels, specifically those who represent God's judicial power and stability.</note> are made of fire.

<margin>k</margin> For this reason, I think it is worthy of **intellectual attention** <note>original: "noeras epistaseōs," a focused application of the mind to spiritual truths rather than just a casual reading.</note>, that the tradition of the <term>Sacred Oracles</term> <note>original: "logiōn," a term Dionysius uses to refer to the Holy Scriptures as divine utterances.</note> regarding the angels says that they are "a thousand thousands" and "ten thousand times ten thousand." <margin>A</margin> This illumination, perfected by the **Godhead’s** <term>Godhead</term> <note>original: "thearchias," the divine source of all authority and power.</note> own exalted causes for all sacred minds in **supersubstantial** <note>original: "hyperousiō," meaning a reality that exists beyond all created categories of being or essence.</note> hiddenness, is somehow more manifest to the powers standing around it <note>The "powers standing around" are the highest order of angels, like the Seraphim, who are closest to the divine source.</note>, and it reveals and distributes itself to them more fully.

# Dionysius on the Celestial Hierarchy

...they stretch upward in a **good-like** manner <note>original: "agathoeidōs." ### Of Dionysius, concerning the...

...of him who was purified for divine obedience, they say that it was not spoken by one of those beings established directly around God, but by one of the purifying powers set over us.

<margin>E</margin> However, another person offered me an explanation for the present objection that was not at all out of place. For he said that that great angel—whoever he was—who fashioned the vision to initiate the **Theologian** <note>original: "theologon." The power of the Godhead as the absolute source of all order and hierarchy.</term> power, visiting all things, proceeds through all and permeates all things without being held fast, yet remains hidden to all again—not only as being transcendently set apart from all things, but also as secretly sending its providential energies upon all—so too does it appear proportionately to all intellectual beings. By handing over its own **gift of light** <note>original: "phōtodosian."</note> to the most senior beings, it naturally distributes that light through them...

# CHAPTER 11

## Why all the heavenly essences are collectively called "heavenly powers."

Now that these things have been defined, it is worth considering the reason why we are accustomed to call all the angelic <term>essences</term> <note>original: "ousiai." # The Celestial Hierarchy.

## CHAPTER IX.

<margin>P</margin> **Concerning the Principalities, the Archangels, and the Angels; and concerning their final hierarchy.**

<margin>L</margin> there remains for our contemplation that sacred rank which concludes the angelic hierarchies; the one composed of the god-like **Principalities**, the **Archangels**, and the **Angels**. And first, I think it is necessary to explain, as far as I am able, the revelations found in their holy names. 

For the name of the heavenly **Principalities** <note>original: "archai." These are the first rank of the third triad.</note> reveals their god-like authority and leadership within a sacred order, as is most fitting for princely powers. It shows that they are turned entirely toward the **Beginning** <term>Beginning</term><note>original: "archēn." It reveals that they are shaped, as much as possible, after that very Source who creates all beginnings, and that they manifest His super-essential leadership through the good order of their princely powers.

<margin>T</margin> The rank of the holy **Archangels** is of the same order as the heavenly **Principalities**. For, as I have said, there is one hierarchy and rank that includes them and the **Angels**.

## The Celestial Hierarchy

...not two properties. I believe, then, that the revelatory name of the holy **Dominions** <note>original: "kyriotētōn." This is the first rank of the second celestial triad. Light and knowledge proceeding directly from the Divine.</note> granted to them; instead, they are powerfully led upward to the imitation of God. They do not abandon their god-like movement through any lack of manliness, but look unswervingly toward the <term>super-essential</term> <note>original: "hyperousion." A core Dionysian term meaning "beyond being" or "above all essence," used to describe the nature of God which exceeds human language.</note> and power-bestowing Power. They become, as far as possible, a powerful image of that Power, turned toward it as the source of all strength, while also proceeding toward the lower ranks to bestow power in a god-like manner.

# [Of] Dionysius on the Celestial [Hierarchy]

I marvel that even the first of the celestial beings—who are the very highest and so far above all others—submissively desire the divine-ruling <note>original: "thearchikōn." This refers to the power or light that comes directly from God as the supreme Ruler.</note> illuminations as if they were beings of the middle rank. For they do not immediately ask: "Why are your garments red?" <note>A reference to Isaiah 63:2. Dionysius interprets this as the highest angels questioning the Christ as he ascends to heaven after the Passion.</note> Rather, they first doubt and question among themselves, showing that they are eager to learn and desire the divine-working <note>original: "theourgikēs." Knowledge of God’s direct actions or "works" in the world, such as the Incarnation.</note> knowledge, yet they do not anticipate the illumination that is granted according to the divine progression.

Thus, the first hierarchy of heavenly minds is initiated by the Source of Initiation <note>original: "teletarchias." This refers to God as the author of all sacred rites and perfections.</note> itself. Because it reaches out directly to this Source, it is filled—in a measure appropriate to its nature—with the most holy purification of the boundless light of the pre-perfecting rite. It is thereby purified, enlightened, and perfected; it is free from all diminishment <note>literally "mixing with lower things."</note>, full of the primary light, and made a participant in the first-given knowledge and science. 

To put it briefly, I might say this not without reason: that the participation in divine-ruling science is itself purification, enlightenment, and perfection. It purifies from ignorance, as it were, by the knowledge of the more perfect initiations <note>original: "mueseōn." Sacred mysteries or teachings.</note> granted according to the merit of the being. It <margin>doubt/difficulty <note>original: "apor..." likely an abbreviation for "aporia" or questioning.</note></margin> enlightens by this same divine knowledge, through which it also purifies the mind that did not previously behold the things now made manifest through the higher illumination. Finally, it perfects that same mind by that same light, through the established knowledge of the most luminous initiations. This, then, according to my knowledge, is the first rank of heavenly beings which...

# The Celestial Hierarchy

# Dionysius, on the [Celestial Hierarchy]

...[unaffected] by material images, but as being purely higher than any state of falling away; <margin>H</margin> and transcending every subordinate sacred thing according to the most supreme purity. ## [On the] Celestial Hierarchy

[The Cherubim are] second through the outpouring of the gifted wisdom. <note>original: "ta deutera tēi chysei tēs dōrētheisēs sophias." This refers to the etymology of the name "Cherubim," which Dionysius interprets as a "fullness of knowledge" flowing from God.</note>

They are established firmly and unshakably around the truly Highest One with all their powers. They are receptive to the divine outflowing <term>thearchikēs apophytēseōs: the process by which God’s life and power "grafted" onto or flowed into the angels at their creation</term> in a state of total peace and immateriality. **This** then is the explanation of their names as they have been revealed to us. Now we must say what we consider their hierarchy to be. Now, I pray that I may speak worthily of how the hierarchy of the most supreme minds <note>original: "hypertatōn noōn" - referring to the highest angels as pure intellects.</note> is revealed through the Holy Oracles. These first beings are established immediately after the Godhead <term>thearchia: the source of divinity, often referring to the Trinity as the "Origin of Godhead"</term> who gave them their being. It is as if they are stationed in the very entrance-hall of the Divine. They have surpassed every created power, both invisible and visible. We must consider their hierarchy to be entirely of the same kind and character as their own nature.

# Dionysius on the Celestial Hierarchy

This is why those who know the Hebrew language say the name [Seraphim] signifies either "burners" or "heaters," whereas the name of the **Cherubim** signifies a "fullness of knowledge" or an "outpouring of wisdom." <note>original: "plēthos gnōseōs ē chysin sophias." Dionysius relies on a traditional but linguistically creative etymology where "Cherub" is linked to the idea of knowledge flowing like a stream.</note> It is fitting, therefore, that the first of the celestial hierarchies is ministered by the most exalted beings, possessing a rank higher than all others, since it is established immediately around God. The primary "theophanies" <term>theophania: a visible manifestation of God to humankind or heavenly beings</term> and initiations of perfection are channeled through this hierarchy first, as it is the most proximate to the Source. Thus, they are named "Heaters," "Thrones," and "Outpouring of Wisdom"—names which illustratively reveal their godlike dispositions.

<margin>The</margin> The name of the **Seraphim** clearly teaches us their ever-moving stability around divine things; their heat, sharpness, and the "boiling" intensity <note>original: "hyperzeon." This describes an intense, bubbling spiritual energy or fervor.</note> of their ceaseless, unwavering, and constant motion. It reflects their power to actively liken those below them to themselves by "reheating" them and rekindling a similar warmth. It also points to their ability to purify through a lightning-like and total consumption of dross, and their light-giving and illuminating quality which is both open and unquenchable—always staying the same, driving away and annihilating every kind of dark and gloomy shadow. 

<margin>The</margin> The name of the **Cherubim** denotes their power to know and behold God, and their capacity to receive the highest gift of light. It signifies their ability to contemplate the <term>thearchikēs: belonging to the Divine Source or "God-rule"</term> beauty in its original, productive power. Through this, they are filled with the gift of wisdom, and they communicate this wisdom generously to

## CHAPTER 4.
### What the name of "angels" signifies.

**S**ince, then, the nature of hierarchy itself has, I believe, been well defined by us, we must next celebrate the angelic hierarchy. We must contemplate their sacred **molds** <note>original: "morphopoiïas." Dionysius refers to the symbolic forms or "shapes" given to angels in the Bible to help human minds understand them.</note> as they are described in the Scriptures with **super-cosmic** <term>super-cosmic (hyperkosmiōs): a perspective that looks beyond the physical universe to the spiritual reality</term> eyes, so that we may be led up to their most godlike simplicity through these mystical representations. Let us praise the Beginning of all hierarchical knowledge with a reverence that befits God, and with thanksgivings for His initiating work.

<margin>P</margin> First of all, it is a true word to say that the **super-essential** <term>super-essential (hyperousios): existing beyond the very category of "being" or "substance"</term> Godhead, having established the essences of all things by His goodness, brought them into being. For it is the unique property of the Cause of all things and of the Goodness that is beyond all things to call all beings into fellowship with Himself, in the way that each being is defined by its own particular capacity.

<margin>P</margin> Therefore, all things that exist participate in a **Providence** <note>original: "pronoia." The divine care and forethought God exercises over the universe.</note> which flows out from the super-essential and all-causing Divinity. For they would not exist at all unless they participated in the essence and the Beginning of all things. All inanimate things participate in it by their very existence, for the "being" of all things is the Divinity, which is beyond being.

## THE CELESTIAL HIERARCHY

...illumination, and perfection. It is beyond purification, beyond light, and is **pre-perfect** <note>original: "proteleios." Existing in a state of completion before any other thing was made.</note>; it is the **source of all initiation** <note>original: "autoteletarchia." The self-subsisting origin of all sacred rites and perfections.</note>. It is the cause of every hierarchy and is transcendently set apart from every sacred thing by its excellence.

I believe it is necessary, then, that those who are being **purified** <term>purification (katharsis): the first stage of the spiritual path, involving the removal of material distractions and "unlikeness" to God</term> should be made entirely unmixed and freed from all discordant confusion.

<margin>b 5</margin> Those who are being **illuminated** <term>illumination (photismos): the second stage, where the mind is filled with divine light and the power to contemplate spiritual truths</term> should be filled with divine light, directed toward a habit and power of contemplation, being led upward by the all-pure eyes of the mind.

Those who are being **perfected** <note>original: "teloumenous." Those undergoing the final stage of initiation or "perfection."</note>—reshaped from a state of incompleteness—should become partakers of the perfecting knowledge of the sacred things they have witnessed.

Furthermore, the **purifiers** must, out of their abundance of purification, share their own purity with others.

The **illuminators**—as more transparent minds, naturally suited to receive and share the light, and being blessedly filled with sacred radiance—should channel the light overflowing within them toward those worthy of receiving it.

<margin>8</margin> The **perfectors** <note>original: "telestourgous." Those who perform the rites of perfection or spiritual completion.</note>, as those who possess the knowledge of how to impart initiation, should initiate those being perfected into the most holy mystery of the knowledge of the sacred things they have beheld.

<margin>8</margin> Therefore, each rank in the hierarchical order is led up, according to its own capacity, toward a **divine cooperation** <term>divine cooperation (theia synergia): the concept that created beings act as "fellow workers" with God to distribute grace</term>. It performs, through grace and a God-given power, those things which belong to the **Thearchy** <term>Thearchy (thearchia): the divine source of all authority, holiness, and the "rule of God"</term> naturally and beyond nature. These things are performed transcendently by God, yet are brought into the reachable imitation of God-loving minds.

## DIONYSIUS ON THE HIE<gloss>RARCHY</gloss>

...shining, according to the laws of the **Godhead** <term>Godhead (Thearchy): the divine source and principle of all things, usually referring to the Holy Trinity as the origin of all sacred order</term>. For it is not permitted for those who conduct sacred rites, nor for those being sacredly initiated, to act at all against the sacred ordinances of their own **source of initiation** <note>original: "teletarchia." The foundational principle or authority that governs a specific sacred rite.</note>.

<margin>T</margin> Furthermore, they cannot even exist in any other way than by longing for that divine splendor itself, looking toward it with sacred devotion, and being reshaped according to the **capacity** <note>original: "analogia." Not just a comparison, but the specific "proportion" or "receptive ability" of an individual soul or angel to receive divine light.</note> of each of the sacred minds.

Therefore, when one speaks of "Hierarchy," they mean a certain sacred order as a whole, an image of the beauty of the Godhead. In its hierarchical ranks and sciences, it performs the mysteries of its own illumination, being assimilated to its own source as much as is permitted. 

For the **perfection** <note>original: "teleiosis." The final state of spiritual completion or "fulfillment."</note> of each of those assigned to a hierarchy is to be led upward, according to their own capacity, toward the **imitation of God** <note>original: "theomimiton." The process of becoming like God through virtue and contemplation.</note>. And what is more divine than all, as the **Scriptures** <note>original: "logia." Literally "the oracles," referring to the Bible.</note> say, is to become a "fellow-worker" with God, and to show the divine energy appearing in oneself as far as possible.

<margin>Ξ</margin> For instance, since the order of hierarchy is that some are being purified while others purify, and some are being illuminated while others illuminate, and some are being perfected while others initiate, the imitation of God will be appropriate to each in this manner: 

The divine blessedness—to speak in human terms—is entirely unmixed with any "unlikeness" and is full of eternal light. It is perfect and in need of no perfection, **purifying, illuminating, and initiating** <note>The three-fold action of God that the hierarchy mirrors on earth and in heaven.</note>.

## What hierarchy is, and what benefit there is in having a hierarchy.

<margin>E</margin> Hierarchy is, in my opinion, a sacred order, a science, and an activity, being made like the **divine-form** <note>original: "theoeides." This refers to having the "shape" or "form" of God, not physically, but in character and spirit.</note> as far as is attainable. It shares its own light with each according to their worth, and it brings them to perfection in a most divine rite, according to the harmonious and unchanging formation of those being initiated toward itself.

<margin>S</margin> The goal of a hierarchy, therefore, is the assimilation and union with God, as far as possible. It holds Him as the leader of every sacred science and activity. By looking unwaveringly at His most divine beauty, it is shaped as much as possible after Him, and it makes its own followers into divine images: mirrors most clear and without blemish, receptive to the **primordial light** <note>original: "archiphōtou." # Dionysius on the <unclear>Celestial Hierarchy</unclear>

For since <gloss>indeed</gloss>, as the secret and priestly tradition has taught, we truly say that [the Divine] is not like any existing thing, we are yet ignorant of its **super-essential** <note>original: "hyperousion," a term describing God as existing far beyond the nature or "essence" of created things</note> and unthinkable and unutterable infinity. Therefore, if **negations** <note>original: "apophaseis," the practice of describing God by what He is not</note> regarding divine matters are true, while **affirmations** <note>original: "kataphaseis," the practice of giving God positive names like "Good" or "Light"</note> are inadequate, then the manifestation of invisible things through **dissimilar representations** is much more suitable to the secrecy of things unutterable.

<margin>T</margin>**T**hus the sacred writings of the scriptures honor the celestial orders—not by filling them with shameful images—but by making them manifest through dissimilar shapes, thereby demonstrating that they have transcended all material things in a way that is beyond this world.

<margin>O</margin>**O**nly those who think clearly would agree, I believe, that images which are unlike [the divine] lead our minds upward much better than those which resemble it. For in the case of the more "honorable" sacred symbols, it is likely that people might be led astray, imagining that the celestial beings are some kind of **golden** entities, or shining men, dazzling and beautiful, dressed in radiant clothing and flashing with harmless fire, or any other such beautiful forms with which theology has characterized the celestial minds.

<margin>O</margin>**O**rderly and uplifting wisdom, used by holy theologians, descends to these unlike representations precisely so that those who have not conceived of anything higher than visible beauties might not suffer this [misunderstanding]. # CHAPTER 2.

## That divine and celestial things are fittingly revealed even through dissimilar symbols.

<meta>This page continues the argument from Chapter 2. While the previous page warned against taking biblical metaphors too literally (like imagining angels as literal birds or beasts), this page explains the positive purpose of these symbols: they serve as a necessary "bridge" or "hand-holding" for the human mind to transition from the physical world to the spiritual realm.</meta>

->[OF THE] CELESTIAL HIERARCHY<-
<note>original: "οὐρανίας ἱεραρχίας." This is the running header of the book.</note>

->[c ii]<-
<note>This is a "signature mark," used by early printers to keep the pages in the correct order for binding.</note>

...deeming [our hierarchy] worthy of a **super-worldly** <note>literally "hyper-cosmic," meaning existing beyond the physical universe</note> imitation of the celestial hierarchies. By diversifying the immaterial hierarchies with material shapes and formal compositions, Scripture has handed them down to us. This was done so that, in a way proportionate to our own nature, we might be led upward from these most sacred fashioned-forms to the simple, formless elevations and likenesses. 

For it is not possible for our human mind to be extended toward that immaterial imitation and contemplation of the celestial hierarchies unless it uses the **material guidance** <term>material guidance: "hylaia cheiragogia," literally "material hand-holding." A key concept in Dionysius where physical objects "lead us by the hand" to God</term> suited to it. It must consider visible beauties as icons of invisible loveliness, and sensory fragrances as imprints of the **intellectual distribution** <note>original: "noētēs diadosis" — the way God "spreads" or "distributes" his presence into the mind</note> of God. 

It must see material lights as an image of the immaterial gift of light, and the detailed sacred teachings of the priests as a reflection of the mind's own contemplative fulfillment. We should view the orderly arrangements of our ceremonies here on earth as a way to reach a harmonious and ordered habit toward divine things. Furthermore, we should see the participation in the most divine **Eucharist** <note>literally "thanksgiving," referring to the central Christian rite of communion</note> as a way of sharing in the fellowship of Jesus. In short, all those things that are given to the celestial beings in a **super-worldly** manner are handed down to us through symbols.

<margin>T</margin>herefore, for the sake of this proportionate **deification** <term>deification: "theosis." The process of becoming "god-like" or united with God through grace</term> of ours, the benevolent **Source of Rites** <term>Source of Rites: "Teletarchia." A title for God or Christ as the one who initiates and perfects all sacred ceremonies</term> has revealed the celestial hierarchies to us. By making our own earthly hierarchy a "fellow-minister" with them through this likeness—as far as our power allows—the Source has described the super-celestial beings through sensory images in the holy scriptures.

### VOCABULARY
*   **Celestial hierarchies**: The ordered ranks of angels in heaven.
*   **Imitation**: The process by which a lower rank tries to mirror the qualities of a higher rank.
*   **Immaterial things**: Realities that have no physical body or "matter."
*   **Intellectual distribution**: The way spiritual truths are shared or spread into the human intellect.
*   **Most divine Eucharist**: The sacrament of the Lord's Supper, viewed here as a way for humans to participate in the life of Jesus.
*   **Source of Rites**: The divine principle that establishes and governs all sacred rituals.
*   **Deification**: The ultimate goal of the soul, which is to be made like God.

<summary>Dionysius explains that material symbols—like light, fragrance, and the Eucharist—are necessary tools that "lead the human mind by the hand" toward immaterial spiritual truths. He argues that the earthly church hierarchy is a symbolic mirror of the angelic hierarchy in heaven, designed to help humans achieve deification.</summary>
<keywords>celestial hierarchy, symbols, theosis, deification, Eucharist, Jesus, contemplation, spiritual guidance, angels</keywords>

# [THE WRITINGS] OF DIONYSIUS CONCERNING THE [CELESTIAL HIERARCHY]
<note>original: "Διονυσίου περὶ τῆς." The title is truncated in the OCR but refers to "Dionysius on the Celestial Hierarchy."</note>

Therefore, having called upon Jesus—the Fatherly Light, the Being, the True [Light] who illuminates every person coming into the world; through whom we have obtained our access to the Father, the Source of Light—let us look upward, as far as is possible, toward the illuminations of the most sacred scriptures handed down from our fathers. Let us, as best we can, contemplate the hierarchies of the celestial minds which have been revealed to us by those scriptures in a symbolic and **uplifting** <term>uplifting: "anagogically," a method of spiritual interpretation that leads the mind from earthly symbols to heavenly truths</term> manner. 

And having received the primal and more-than-primal gift of light from the Divine Father—which reveals to us the most blessed hierarchies of the angels in figurative symbols—let us, with the immaterial and steady eyes of the mind, be stretched upward again from this light toward its simple <margin>once</margin> <note>original: "pote." This marginal note likely refers to a textual variant or emphasizes the eventual "once-and-for-all" nature of the union.</note> ray. For indeed, this light never truly loses its own unique unity. Even though it is graciously multiplied and goes forth to produce an uplifting and unifying blend for those under its care, it remains inwardly and firmly fixed within itself in an unmoving identity. And those who stretch toward it, as is right, it stretches upward in return and unifies them according to its own simplifying union.

**F**or it is not possible for the **Divine Ray** <term>Divine Ray: "thearchikē aktis," the beam of light or energy proceeding from the "Thearchy" (the source of the Divine) to the creation</term> to shine upon us in any other way than by being wrapped in a variety of sacred veils <note>original: "parapetasmasin," literally curtains or hangings used in a temple to shroud a mystery</note>, and being prepared for us by **Fatherly providence** <margin>Fatherly providence</margin> in a way that is natural and appropriate to our human condition. For this reason, the sacred institution of our own most holy hierarchy [has been established] by the **Master of the Rites**...

<vocab>Dionysius Areopagita, Celestial Hierarchy, light (φῶς), hierarchy (ἱεραρχία), union (ἕνωσις), angels (ἀγγέλων), providence (πρόνοια)</vocab>

<summary>In this opening chapter, the author invokes Jesus as the "Fatherly Light" and explains that divine truth can only reach the human mind through "sacred veils" or symbols provided by God's providence. This establishes the central theme: the use of physical things to lead the soul to an immaterial, spiritual union with God.</summary>

# POPE LEO X

## To our beloved sons Philip Giunta and his sons, Florentine Booksellers.

**B**eloved sons, Health and Apostolic Blessing. <note>original: "Salutem & Aplicam beñ."; a standard papal salutation abbreviated from "Salutem et Apostolicam benedictionem"</note>

We consider it just that the Apostolic See <term>Apostolic See: the office and jurisdiction of the Pope, the central government of the Catholic Church</term>, over which we preside by the Lord's authority, should not only offer the right hand of its help to those who never cease to labor for the public good—especially in literary matters—but also, by kindly receiving them under the shield of its protection, should never cease to encourage them to continue and increase labors of this kind.

Since, therefore, as you have had explained to us, you possess a **Latin Plato** <note>referring to the translations of Plato's works, likely those by Marsilio Ficino, which the Giunta family sought to print in a superior edition</note> and many other books, both Latin and Greek, far better than those which are commonly circulated, and you desire to print them and thereby expand literary learning and bring aid to those students striving toward the highest peak of the sciences, yet you fear lest others, as soon as the books have been printed and issued by you, might cause you the greatest financial loss by reprinting those same books.

We, who from our earliest youth have always loved the study of literature and wish to bring help to those who love it, [support] you in this laudable [project]... <meta>The text breaks off at "p", likely the beginning of "proposito" (purpose) or "project." The catchword at the bottom "p" confirms the continuation to the next page.</meta>

## POPE LEO X

-> To our beloved son Filippo Giunta and <-
-> his associate Florentine Booksellers. <-

> Beloved son, Health and Apostolic Blessing. <note>original: "Salutem & Apostolicam Ben."; the standard opening for a papal brief, abbreviated in the original Latin.</note>

Since literary labors never cease to work for the public good—and without their support, other branches of learning (over which we preside by the Lord’s authority) would surely fail—it is only right that we should not only offer the aid of our favor but also grant them the shield of our protection. By doing so, we never cease to encourage the commendation and growth of such efforts.

Therefore, it has been explained to us on your behalf that you intend to print Greek and many other Latin books which are extremely useful to readers. Because you desire to bring aid to those striving toward the highest peak of the sciences, it is right that learning should be properly advanced through your work. Yet, you are concerned that because these books require significant investment for their initial scholarly revision and the tools of the printing trade, others might cause you the greatest financial loss <note>This refers to "book piracy," where rival printers would quickly copy a new edition, undercutting the original publisher who had paid for the scholarly editing.</note>.

We, who have always loved and fostered the study of literature and the means by which it is advanced from our earliest years, wish to meet your laudable desires with opportune... <unclear>...</unclear>

<margin>Symbol</margin> <note>original: "symbolon"</note> something perceived by the senses, taken in place of something perceived by the mind; for instance, instead of the immaterial and divine nourishment and joy, bread and wine and such things. <note>This definition reflects the Neoplatonic view of physical sacraments as "symbols" of higher spiritual realities.</note>
<margin>Having taken together</margin> <note>original: "sunelōn"</note> having grasped, having gathered.
<margin>Collectively</margin> <note>original: "sullēbdēn"</note> gathered together, under one, at once.
<margin>In this way</margin> <note>original: "tautē"</note> thus.
<margin>This same</margin> <note>original: "tautēn"</note> similar, equal, the very same.
<margin>Rite</margin> <note>original: "teletē"</note> of the mysteries, from the word for "perfected"; a completion or perfecting.
<margin>Source of the rites</margin> <note>original: "teletarchia"</note> the leader of the rites, or the one presiding over those being initiated. <note>A term frequently used by Dionysius to describe God or a high-ranking celestial/ecclesiastical power.</note>
<margin>Sometime</margin> <note>original: "pote"</note> used instead of the word for "when?"
<margin>Swine</margin> <note>original: "huas"</note> pigs.
<margin>Open-air</margin> <note>original: "hupaithros"</note> under the sky.

**Vocabulary List:**
Cowering, may we be revered, it folds together, symbol, collectively, rite, source of the rites, swine, open-air.

...[asserting that] pagan wisdom <note>original: τῆς ἔξωθεν σοφίας (tes exothen sophias); literally "the wisdom from without," referring to secular or Greek philosophy</note> steals our own ideas. <margin>1</margin> But since some people claim that the work does not belong to the Saint, but to someone of a later generation, they must necessarily conclude that he committed forbidden and absurd acts, fabricating such details about himself <margin>3</margin> as if he had been present with the Apostles and had written letters to them—men with whom, according to these critics, he never actually lived nor corresponded. <margin>3</margin> They also claim that he fabricated a prophecy addressed to the Apostle John <margin>3</margin> while John was in exile, saying that he would return again to the land of Asia and teach as he was accustomed to do. <margin>6</margin> They argue this is the behavior of a teller of tall tales <note>original: τερατολόγου (teratologou); a narrator of marvels or monsters, implying one who exaggerates the truth</note> who is madly hunting for the reputation of a prophet. 

<margin>6</margin> They also point to his claim that at the very time of the Savior’s Passion, while he was staying in Heliopolis <note>The "City of the Sun" in Egypt</note>, <margin>4</margin> he was with **Apollophanes** <note>A fellow philosopher whom Dionysius allegedly befriended in Egypt</note> observing and philosophizing together regarding the solar eclipse, noting that it had not occurred in a natural way or according to the usual patterns of that time. <margin>5</margin> Furthermore, he says that he was present alongside the Apostles at the funeral procession <note>original: προκομιδῇ (prokomide); the ritual transport of the body</note> of the holy remains of the <term>Theotokos</term> <note>original: Θεοτόκος; a Greek title for Mary meaning "God-bearer" or Mother of God</note> Mary, <margin>3</margin> and that he offered the sayings of **Hierotheus**, his own teacher, from the funeral orations written for her. 

They argue that to fabricate letters and discourses as if they were delivered to the disciples of the Apostles <margin>5</margin> is an act worthy of great absurdity and condemnation—even for an ordinary person, let alone for a man who had been raised to such a high level <margin>4</margin> in character and knowledge that he surpassed all sensible things and was joined to intellectual beauties, and through them, as far as possible, to God. <margin>5</margin>

<meta>This page continues the defense of the authenticity of the Dionysian corpus. # SCHOLIA. I.

<margin>10</margin> Note how some of the "outside" philosophers <note>original: τῶν ἔξω (ton exo); a standard term for pagan or secular thinkers outside the Christian faith</note>—and <margin>1</margin> especially **Proclus**—frequently utilized the theorems of the blessed **Dionysius**, even using his very words in their plainest sense. One might suspect from this that long ago, the later philosophers in Athens stole his treatises (as recorded in this present book) and hid them, so that they themselves might appear to be the "fathers" of these divine words. But through the providence of God, the present treatise has now come to light to expose their vanity and trickery, and to show that it is a habit of theirs to steal what belongs to us. 

The divine **Basil** teaches this; for regarding the phrase "In the beginning was the Word," he says the following: "I know that many of those who are outside the Word of Truth, but who take great pride in worldly wisdom, have admired these things and dared to include them in their own compositions." For the devil is a thief and carries our secrets to his own prophets. So it is with this.

<margin>t</margin> Furthermore, regarding **Numenius the Pythagorean**—who openly says, "For what is **Plato**, but **Moses** speaking Attic?" <note>original: Μωσῆς ἀττικίζων (Moses attikizon); meaning Moses speaking the refined Greek dialect of Athens</note>—no one can deny this, as he was not one of ours but belonged to the opposition. This is also testified by **Eusebius**, the former leader of **Caesarea** in Palestine. This practice of theirs was common, not only now, but even before the coming of **Christ**.

<summary>This page argues that the similarities between Dionysius the Areopagite and pagan Neoplatonists like Proclus exist because the pagans "stole" divine Christian truths. It cites St. Basil and Numenius to support the idea that Greek philosophy is often just a derivative of older, biblical wisdom.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the discussion of Dionysius the Areopagite's social standing and the historical composition of the high court of Athens, citing classical historians to validate his status. It concludes by explaining the mythological origins of the name "Areopagus."</meta>

...of the **God-bearing author** <note>original: θεοφόρος (theophoros); a title given to authors believed to be inspired by or carrying the Spirit of God</note>, with his rank also having been added.

<margin>Φ</margin> For he says "Areopagite," but I would further suggest that because of his exceptional wisdom and his distinguished, blameless civic life among the Athenians, it was necessary for him to be memorialized along with his household. For one must know, as I stated before, that it was not within the power of just any man to serve in the Council of the Areopagus. Rather, those who were the leaders among the Athenians—distinguished in lineage, wealth, and virtuous life, and established as eminent in these respects—served as counselors in the Council of the Areopagus.

<margin>Ε</margin> For it was from the nine established **Archons** <term>Archontes; the highest-ranking magistrates or rulers in ancient Athens</term> that the Areopagite judges had to be appointed, as **Androtion** <note>An Athenian historian (c. 410–340 BCE) who wrote about the laws and history of the city.</note> says in the second book of his *Atthides* <note>The "Atthides" were local histories or chronicles of Attica, the region surrounding Athens.</note>. Later, the Council of the Areopagus came to consist of more members—that is, of fifty-one of the most illustrious men—provided they were from the **Eupatridai** <term>Eupatridai; the "well-born" hereditary aristocrats of Athens</term> (as we said) and excelled in wealth and a sober life, as **Philochorus** <note>A prominent historian and researcher of Athenian traditions (c. 340–260 BCE).</note> records through the third book of his own *Atthides*.

<margin>Ε</margin> The court of the Areopagus was located outside the city and was named as follows: according to what the Athenians tell in their myths, it was named from the court established on that very prominence of the mountain near the city during the dispute between **Poseidon** and **Ares**.

<margin>Ο</margin> For Poseidon brought a legal case against Ares according to the ancient myths of the Athenians, claiming in this place that his own son, **Halirrhothius**, had been slain.

# ->PROLOGUE TO THE<-
# ->BLESSED DIONYSIUS.<-

<margin>Τ</margin> **T**he noble birth and the conspicuous wealth of the great Dionysius is demonstrated by the Athenian council itself, in which he was chosen to serve as a counselor. For he happened to be one of the Areopagites <note>Members of the high court of Athens</note>, as the divine Luke declared when recording the sacred deeds <note>The Book of Acts</note> of the holy apostles.

<margin>Ξ</margin>
<margin>Ε</margin> For having stated that the most holy Apostle Paul arrived in Athens and engaged with certain men of the learned Epicurean philosophers and those of the Stoa <term>Stoics; a school of philosophy that taught that virtue is the only good and emphasized endurance and reason</term>; and having preached faith in the Lord Jesus Christ, the resurrection of the dead, and the universal judgment, Paul was seized by those who were un-philosophical <note>original: ἀφιλοσόφων (aphilosophōn); here used to describe those who lacked true spiritual wisdom or were hostile to the Gospel</note> and led to the Areopagus <note>Mars Hill, the meeting place of the high court</note>. After making a public speech, he immediately won some over and brought them toward the light of truth; the text adds: “And so Paul went out from among them.”

<margin>Ξ</margin>

<margin>Τ</margin> "But some men joined him and believed; among whom also was Dionysius the Areopagite, and a woman named Damaris, and others with them" <note>A direct quotation of Acts 17:34</note>.

<margin>Ο</margin>
<margin>Ε</margin> I, therefore, do not think it is without reason that, out of all those who believed at that time through the divine Paul, only the most excellent Dionysius is named by the writer <note>Luke, the author of Acts</note>...

# THE CELESTIAL HIERARCHY
## CHAPTER I

->That every divine illumination, though it proceeds to created things in various ways, remains one and simple in itself, and turns those it illuminates back toward its own unity.<-

"Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, coming down from the Father of Lights." <margin>James 1:17</margin> <note>The author begins with a quotation from the Epistle of James, establishing the theological premise that all knowledge and "light" originate from God.</note> 

Furthermore, every manifestation of light that is set in motion by the Father, and which reaches out to us with such generosity, acts as a unifying power. It fills us anew and draws us upward, turning us back toward the oneness of the Father who gathers all things, and toward a divine simplicity. For as the scriptures say, *From Him, and through Him, and in Him all things exist.* <margin>Romans 11:36</margin> <note>original: "Ex ipso enim, et per ipsum, et in ipso sunt omnia."</note>

### Section I

We must, therefore, invoke Jesus—the Light of the Father, the <insert>True Light</insert> <gloss>The Word of God</gloss> who illuminates every person coming into this world—through whom we have gained access to the Father, the primordial Source of Light. <note>This "Source of Light" refers to the Neoplatonic idea of the "One" from which all existence flows.</note>

**Foundational Principles of Light**

| Latin Term | English Translation | Definition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| <term>Pater Luminum</term> | Father of Lights | A biblical title for God, emphasizing Him as the source of both physical stars and spiritual truths. |
| <term>Processio</term> | Procession | The theological concept of divine energy or light flowing outward from God into the universe. |
| <term>Simplicitas</term> | Simplicity | In a philosophical sense, the state of being undivided; God is "simple" because He is not made of parts. |
| <term>Deifica</term> | Deifying / God-making | The process of being made more like God through the reception of divine light. |

<margin>See Dionysius in "The Divine Names," Chapter 4.</margin>

<summary>This page marks the beginning of the treatise, establishing that all spiritual illumination comes from God and serves to draw the soul back to divine unity. It uses the metaphor of light to explain how God interacts with the created world.</summary>

<keywords>illumination, Father of Lights, divine unity, Jesus, spiritual light, Neoplatonism, Dionysius, procession, simplicity</keywords>

# ON THE CELESTIAL HIERARCHY

## CHAPTER II

### That divine and heavenly things are fittingly revealed even through dissimilar symbols.

-> I. <-

I believe it is necessary, therefore, to first explain what we intend by the word <term>hierarchy</term><note>From the Greek *hieros* (sacred) and *arche* (rule). The author uses this term to describe the organized, sacred system of the spiritual world.</note>, and what benefits we believe it bestows upon those who are part of its ranks. Next, we must once again praise the heavenly beings according to the tradition of the <term>scriptures</term><note>original: "eloquiorum." The author refers to the Bible as "holy utterances" or "divine words."</note>.

Finally, we must describe the sacred forms through which the heavenly orders are depicted in the scriptures, and determine what spiritual simplicity we should be led toward through these images. This is to ensure that we do not—like the common crowd—erroneously imagine that the heavenly and divine minds possess many feet and faces, or are shaped in the likeness of oxen and cattle, or resemble predatory lions, or have the curved beaks of eagles or the wings of birds. Nor should we imagine fiery chariots in heaven, or material thrones for the use of the Divine, or horses painted in various colors, or commanders of armies armed with spears, or any of the other various figures handed down to us in the scriptures through a variety of sacred symbols.

<summary>Dionysius begins Chapter II by outlining his plan to define the celestial hierarchy and warns readers not to interpret biblical descriptions of angels as literal, physical depictions.</summary>
<keywords>Pseudo-Dionysius, Celestial Hierarchy, symbolism, scripture, angelic forms, spiritual interpretation, divine imagery</keywords>
